subject: Demo recap + Proposed POC plan — RetailBank
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@retailbank.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@retailbank.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Demo recap + Proposed POC plan — RetailBank

Hi Samira / Olivia,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap from the demo and a proposed POC plan to get us from evaluation -> decision: 

What we covered (quick):
- Retrieval-augmented generation for customer support workflows
- Fine-tuned NER / classification for routing and intent detection
- Cost/latency tradeoffs: batching, KV cache, quantization options
- Observability: per-route latency/cost dashboards and audit logs

High-level POC objective:
- Validate that Redwood can meet RetailBank’s latency, accuracy, and audit/security requirements for the customer support assistant on a production-like subset of traffic.

Initial ask from you: can you confirm the success criteria you care about most (latency, accuracy thresholds, cost envelope, security/audit controls)? Based on that we’ll finalize the success criteria and timeline.

Proposed quick POC (draft):
- Duration: 3–4 weeks (flexible based on your team’s availability)
- Week 0 (prep): NDA/SOW, access provisioning, sample dataset handoff
- Week 1 (setup): Redwood sandbox + model selection, baseline runs, perf/latency profiling
- Week 2 (iterate): model tuning, prompt/template adjustments, run evaluation harness on defined test set
- Week 3 (finalize): run full evaluation, cost analysis, review meeting and next-step recommendation

Ownership (proposed):
- RetailBank: provide sample data, business success criteria, and reviewers
- Redwood: sandbox environment, engineering support, evaluation scripts, daily standup during Week 1–2

Attachments: I’ve attached a short POC proposal and our SOW template for procurement.

Next steps: 
1) Please reply with the success criteria and the people who will own the evaluation on your side.
2) Confirm whether a 3-week POC (kickoff week of Jan 25) works for you.

We’re available to kick off next week — Nikhil and Priyom will lead the technical setup.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 09:15:23 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo recap + Proposed POC plan — RetailBank

Thanks Marissa — great demo and thanks for the clear plan. A few items from our side to make the POC meaningful for our stakeholders:

RetailBank proposed success criteria (draft):
- Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end latency < 200ms for the primary inference path
- Accuracy: Intent classification F1 >= 0.88 on our holdout set; NER precision/recall improvement of at least 8% vs current baseline
- Cost: Projection for 1M tokens/day at or below $X (we’ll share target ranges offline)
- Security/compliance: SSO integration, audit logs for request/response, data-at-rest encryption (KMS), retention controls

Stakeholders / evaluators:
- Samira Khan, Head of Data (owner)
- Olivia Chen, Product Manager (end-user evaluation)
- IT / Security: it-support@retailbank.com (will validate networking/SSO)

Timeline note: We’d prefer a slightly compressed timeline if possible — ideally a 3-week POC with kickoff Jan 25 and a review meeting the week of Feb 15. Can Redwood confirm whether the 3-week cadence will let you hit the perf/accuracy goals?

We can share a redacted sample of the last 30K support transcripts (S3 link) and an internal evaluation rubric by EOD tomorrow. We’ll also need an SOW + procurement contact to start the paperwork.

Thanks — Samira

Subject: Re: Demo recap + Proposed POC plan — RetailBank

Samira — thanks for the clear success criteria and the stakeholder list. Below is an updated POC plan that maps directly to each success criterion and includes owners and KPIs.

Updated POC plan (3-week cadence)
- Kickoff (Mon Jan 25) — 1 hour: confirm objectives, access, and schedule
- Week 1 (Jan 25–29): Provisioning + baseline runs
  - Redwood: sandbox provisioned, initial model selection (we’ll start with medium-size open model + quantized variant for cost testing) — owner: Nikhil
  - RetailBank: deliver redacted sample (30K transcripts) and evaluation rubric — owner: Samira
  - Deliverable: baseline latency/cost numbers and baseline accuracy on provided test set
- Week 2 (Feb 1–5): Iteration and tuning
  - Redwood: tune prompts, run additional fine-tune/adapter experiments if allowed, implement caching/batching configs — owner: Nikhil + Priyom
  - RetailBank: run product-level evaluation on 10% of traffic, provide qualitative feedback — owner: Olivia
  - Deliverable: updated accuracy and perf numbers; preliminary cost projection
- Week 3 (Feb 8–12): Final evaluation + review prep
  - Redwood: full runs, cost analysis, produce dashboard links + audit log samples — owner: Priyom
  - RetailBank: internal review + sign-off meeting scheduling — owner: Samira
  - Deliverable: POC report and recommendation

Mapping to success criteria:
- Latency: we’ll instrument 95th/99th percentiles; bring quantized variants and batching knobs to hit the 200ms target — measurable by baseline vs tuned runs
- Accuracy: we’ll run the exact eval rubric you provide; we’ll include confusion matrices and failure cases for review
- Cost: we’ll provide a model-by-model cost sheet (tokens, VM/GPU, infra) and run a sensitivity analysis for 1M tokens/day
- Security: guidance for SSO + audit logs; we’ll provide temp sandbox creds with access logs and retention controls

Evaluation plan / tooling:
- Redwood will run our evaluation harness against your holdout set (scripted) and share raw results + dashboards. We’ll also document any manual test cases Olivia wants us to include.

Procurement / SOW:
- Attached SOW_template.docx is our standard. If procurement needs changes, we’ll iterate quickly — please share finance contact and I’ll loop in our legal/procurement folks.

Next steps (actionable):
1) Confirm kickoff on Mon Jan 25 — we’ll send a calendar invite for 60 minutes.
2) Samira: share S3 link to redacted sample and the evaluation rubric + procurement contact.
3) Redwood (Nikhil): confirm expected sample size and any redaction guidance.

We’ll be ready to move fast once we have the sample and rubric. Thanks again — excited to partner.

Best,
Marissa
